a16z's Alex Danco and Moses Sternstein on the bear case that GPUs would depreciate fast, what rental rates actually show, and why the data points to scarcity:

Alex: "There is a whole case that people made on both sides of the argument that these things were assets that would depreciate on a schedule. And in the past 18 months, I think what we have learned is that all our assumptions were wrong."

Moses: "GPU rental rates continue to go up. Even as token pricing comes down, you see more and more consumption, and it's causing relative scarcity amongst the GPUs that we have."

"Even for the older GPUs, the A100s, which have been around already for five years, that were supposed to become obsolete... Whether they had 4-year depreciation schedules, 6-year depreciation schedules, they were supposed to be obsolete almost immediately, and that was the original bear case."

"And plainly, they're not... Everybody is priced above what they should be based on their scheduled obsolescence. And that's true of the older models, the A100 and the H100."

@alex_danco @MosesSternstein

The short silver trade is becoming crowded.

Silver's 3-month silver put-call skew is up to -3 points, its highest level since early July.

This metric measures the relative cost of put options to call options and is up +10 points over the last 4 weeks, signaling growing demand for bearish bets on silver prices.

Over the last 12 months, this metric has been higher only 2% of the time.

Meanwhile, speculative investors, including hedge funds and commodity trading advisers (CTAs), sold -$2.2 billion in silver futures over the 3 weeks ending October 13th.

As a result, their net long positioning is down to just +$1.7 billion, the lowest in at least 2 years.

For perspective, this metric stood at +$8.5 billion in December 2025.

Investors are extremely bearish on silver.

BREAKING: The average cost of a family’s annual health insurance premium in the US is up +$1,303 YoY, or +5%, to a record $28,303.

This marks the 4th consecutive annual increase of at least +$1,300.

Over this period, the average annual premium for family coverage has surged +$5,884, or +26%.

To put this into perspective, CPI inflation has risen +13% over the same period, or half as much.

Since 1999, the average health insurance premium for a family has soared +$22,494, or +387%.

This represents an average annual growth rate of +6.1%, well above CPI inflation at +2.6% over the same period.

Health insurance has never been more expensive.

🇧🇷Brazil heads to the polls tomorrow for the final round of its presidential election, and this chart shows three ways markets are pricing the outcome:

🟢 @Kalshi — the odds that Flávio Bolsonaro wins (left axis). Now at 84%, up from ~78% on Friday.

🟠 $EWZ — the Brazil ETF that trades on traditional tails (right axis). It closed Friday at $42.60 and won’t trade again until Monday.

⚪ The Brazil ETF perpetual on @HyperliquidX — a 24/7 crypto-style contract that tracks EWZ (right axis). It’s trading right now at $44.30.

The interesting part is what’s happened since Friday’s close. With US markets shut for the weekend, EWZ is frozen, but the perp has kept moving — up roughly 4% today as the Kalshi odds of a Bolsonaro win climbed. That’s a live read on where EWZ could open Monday, before the stock market can react. Plenty of news still to come before then, not least the vote itself — track it all live on our Hyperliquid and election dashboards on @TheTerminal

We’re a few months into the “higher-quality fundamentals” phase of the market cycle.
